title: Constant-to-completed coefficients on derived-complete categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subset A$ be an ideal. Let $\underline A$ and $\underline{A/I^n}$ be the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, with its canonical map $\underline A\to\widehat A$ and projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $D(\mathcal O)$ denote the derived category of sheaves of modules over a ring sheaf $\mathcal O$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An object $M\in D(\mathcal O)$ is derived $I$-complete if, for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every local section $f\in(I\mathcal O)(U)$, one has $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],M|_U)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; here $\mathcal O_U$ denotes restriction to the slice site over $U$, and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is the sheafification of the presheaf of localizations, placed in degree zero.

The sheaf $\widehat A$ is flat over $\underline A$ (tensoring with it is exact), and for every $n\geq1$ the projection induces a canonical isomorphism $\widehat A/I^n\widehat A\cong\underline{A/I^n}$. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] along $\underline A\to\widehat A$ induces an equivalence
$$D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat A,I\widehat A)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\underline A,I).$$
For every $M\in D(\widehat A)$, restriction of scalars and finite reduction have the canonical comparison isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}(M)\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^n}\cong M\otimes^L_{\widehat A}\underline{A/I^n}$$
in $D(\underline{A/I^n})$, with derived change of rings as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. These isomorphisms commute with $\underline{A/I^{n+1}}\to\underline{A/I^n}$.
Let $\mathcal C'$ be a second small site and define $\underline A'$, $\underline{A/I^n}'$ and $\widehat A'$ there by the same construction. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjoint pair $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Identify $u^{-1}\underline A=\underline A'$ and $u^{-1}\underline{A/I^n}=\underline{A/I^n}'$ by the canonical constant-sheaf maps. Let $c:u^{-1}\widehat A\to\widehat A'$ be the map induced by the finite projections. Write $Lu^*_{\widehat A}$ for derived module pullback along $c$, and $Lu^*_{\underline A}$ for constant-coefficient derived module pullback, computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. For every $M\in D(\widehat A)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Res}'(Lu^*_{\widehat A}M)\otimes^L_{\underline A'}\underline{A/I^n}'\cong Lu^*_{\underline A}(\operatorname{Res}M\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^n}).$$
These isomorphisms are in $D(\underline{A/I^n}')$. They are natural in $M$ and $u$ and commute with the finite quotient transitions. The canonical comparison $Lu^*_{\underline A}\operatorname{Res}M\to\operatorname{Res}'(Lu^*_{\widehat A}M)$ is induced on K-flat representatives by the scalar-extension map $u^{-1}M\to u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}\widehat A}\widehat A'$; its finite reductions are the inverses of the displayed isomorphisms. The quotient maps commute with this comparison.

For a strict inverse sequence of complexes, write $R\lim$ for the total right derived inverse limit: take a K-injective resolution in the category of strict inverse sequences and then its termwise inverse limit; K-injectivity means that maps from acyclic tower complexes are null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. This fixes functorial models of the sequential derived limits [def-weil-derived-limit]. Restriction of scalars identifies the sequential derived limits of the finite-reduction towers above and carries the quotient-tower completion unit to the corresponding constant-coefficient completion unit. More explicitly, for $\mathcal O=\underline A$ or $\widehat A$, put
$$Q_m(\mathcal O)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{a_j^m}\mathcal O]$$
in degrees $[-r,0]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with transition maps multiplication by $a_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor. For $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ the canonical map
$$N\longrightarrow R\lim_m(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}Q_m(\mathcal O))$$
is the derived-completion unit for the local completeness condition in the first paragraph. For these two coefficient sheaves the Koszul completion and $R\lim_n(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\underline{A/I^n})$ are canonically isomorphic, respecting the units; restriction of scalars identifies these isomorphisms. In particular Koszul-derived completeness and the stated local completeness condition agree.

proof.text: Put $R=\underline A$, $B=\widehat A$, $S_n=\underline{A/I^n}$. Constant-module sections supply flat sections, surjective transitions and tensor reductions. The sectionwise adic-limit theorem gives flat $R\to B$ and projection quotients $B/I^nB=S_n$; the section tensor formula also gives $R/I^nR=S_n$.

The ideal $IR$ has finite global generators $a_j$. Step 1 supplies flatness and the induced quotient isomorphism, so the flat ringed-ideal equivalence gives the asserted equivalence for exactly the local internal-Hom completeness predicates.

Construct $LT$ for both quotient towers by the homotopy-presentation lemma. Universal cochain-counit transport gives their prescribed cochain comparisons. Constant towers are exact levelwise; use exact derived factorization and strict derived limits. Apply the augmented-unit lemma with $G=\Delta$, $F=\lim$ and $\eta:p\mapsto1\otimes p$; its normalization is the ordinary projection unit on every complex. The flat common-quotient comparison identifies both reductions on a K-flat $B$-model with $P/I^nP$, giving the $S_n$-linear strict comparisons and quotient cones.

For inverseImageData_exists, first obtain the coherent ring functor, its ring operation graphs, ring-map naturality and natural constant-ring isomorphism from the ring-only inverse-image lemma. For each coefficient ring, the proved private ringTransport_algebraic converts the universal addition and multiplication graph laws into the binary monoidal transport equations. Cancellation of the ring-underlying isomorphism proves the inverse equations, and ringIso_isMonHom supplies the multiplicative unit. The existing explicit imageFunctor constructs module inverse image over that ring. Its underlying comparison is the identity; applying L to the universal addition, zero and scalar-action graphs proves all module graph fields, with the scalar equation using e.hom followed by e.inv equals identity. Select these constructed algebraic lifts. Their unchanged ring-underlying comparisons transfer the supplied ring-map naturality, and assemble InverseImageData with the supplied constant-ring comparison.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module; the ring-only constituent is Tag 00YV in sites.tex.

proof.text: Constant inverse image gives $u^{-1}R=R^\prime$, $u^{-1}S_n=S_n^\prime$. Step 1 on $\mathcal C^\prime$ gives flatness and quotients; $u^{-1}(I^nR)$ generates $I^nR^\prime$, and $c$ commutes with projections. Apply the common-quotient pullback comparison: its stated insertion formula gives the unreduced map, inverse finite reductions, quotient compatibility and identity/composition coherence. For completedFinitePull_existsUnique specifically, ordinaryReducedPull_isIso supplies invertibility before localization. On a flat-term K-flat completed-coefficient complex, flat scalar restriction and pullback preserve the resolving class on both sides. Apply finite scalar extension to the specified derivedPullComparison computation square and use naturality of its computation counit. The ordinary reduced comparison is a degreewise isomorphism, and all computation arrows are invertible; cancellation therefore proves the reduced derived comparison invertible. Resolving-class descent extends this to every derived object. Compose its inverse with finitePull to obtain the requested comparison; cancel finitePull.hom to prove the prescribed inverse equation determines it uniquely.

Tensor balancing gives $B\otimes_R-\dashv U=\operatorname{Res}$ by $f\mapsto(m\mapsto f(1\otimes m))$. Restriction is exact; Step 1 and extension/tensor comparison make extension exact. Flat scalar restriction sends flat-term K-flat models to such models over $R$. Module sheaves are Grothendieck; the strict-tower limit theorem supplies K-injective tower resolutions. Thus all exact-restriction theorem hypotheses hold, with Step 3 supplying presentations and the normalized units $c$, and the ordinary common-quotient tower supplying augmented $\theta$; it identifies limits and actual quotient completion units.

The ringed Koszul reflector identifies the displayed $Q_m$ unit with local derived completion for both rings. Restriction identifies finite direct sums, differentials, transitions and degree-zero units termwise. Step 5 then identifies their derived limits and units.

Apply flat constant tensor of pro-zero cones to $Q_m(A)\to A/I^m$, with $R\to R$ and $R\to B$. Step 1 identifies the quotients. The resulting limit isomorphisms respect Koszul and quotient units; Steps 3, 5 and 6 identify the strict augmentations under restriction, hence these comparisons.
